response.sql: WITH side_counts AS (SELECT o.dealedge, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders AS o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM riskandmargin AS r WHERE r.ordervault = o.recordvault) GROUP BY o.dealedge), side_average AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS mean_n FROM side_counts) SELECT SUM(s.n) AS total_count, AVG(s.n - a.mean_n) AS average_excess FROM side_counts AS s CROSS JOIN side_average AS a WHERE s.n > a.mean_n HAVING COUNT(*) > 0;

assumptions.assumption: Each matched order is counted once, even if it has multiple risk/margin records; the average uses sides with at least one matched order.

alternatives.interpretation: Count each matching risk/margin record and order pair.
alternatives.sql: WITH side_counts AS (SELECT o.dealedge, COUNT(*) AS n FROM riskandmargin AS r JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.dealedge), side_average AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS mean_n FROM side_counts) SELECT SUM(s.n) AS total_count, AVG(s.n - a.mean_n) AS average_excess FROM side_counts AS s CROSS JOIN side_average AS a WHERE s.n > a.mean_n HAVING COUNT(*) > 0;

alternatives.interpretation: Include both documented order sides in the average, assigning zero to a side with no matched orders.
alternatives.sql: WITH sides(dealedge) AS (VALUES ('Buy'), ('Sell')), side_counts AS (SELECT sides.dealedge, COUNT(o.orderspivot) AS n FROM sides LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.dealedge = sides.dealedge AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM riskandmargin AS r WHERE r.ordervault = o.recordvault) GROUP BY sides.dealedge), side_average AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS mean_n FROM side_counts) SELECT SUM(s.n) AS total_count, AVG(s.n - a.mean_n) AS average_excess FROM side_counts AS s CROSS JOIN side_average AS a WHERE s.n > a.mean_n HAVING COUNT(*) > 0;
